title: Set Up Your Fine-Tuning Environment: CPU, Free Colab or a Rented GPU
summary: Where to run a fine-tune and how to set each place up: a laptop with no GPU for small models, free Colab or Kaggle T4s for QLoRA on 1–8B models, and a rented GPU for an hour when you need more. Ends with a complete LoRA run on a CPU that you can check before and after.
objectives: Pick a model size and method that fit your hardware using bytes per parameter and the 4N-per-token time estimate
Set up a CPU-only Python environment and run a smoke test that measures seconds per step and extrapolates run time
Run QLoRA on a free Colab or Kaggle T4 with fp16, Drive or Hub checkpoints, and resume after a disconnect
Estimate the cost of a rented GPU run, including setup and idle time, and shut it down safely
Fine-tune SmolLM2-135M-Instruct with LoRA on a laptop and verify the change with a held-out before/after score
prerequisites: Memory per parameter and the LoRA parameter count from [Start Here](/learn/fine-tuning/start-here/sizing-your-first-run); the LoRA update and NF4 from [LoRA and QLoRA](/learn/fine-tuning/peft-lora); chat templates and loss masking from [Instruction Tuning](/learn/fine-tuning/instruction-tuning). Basic Python and a terminal.
